skills.title: Hear and say rhyming word pairs (bell/well, hill/still)
Say the cycle rhyme with its beat and actions
Name bicycle parts and outdoor action words (bell, wheel, seat, pedal, ride)
Say a simple sentence about my own outdoor play

expectations: Says the rhyme lines in order with the clap beat
Picks out at least one rhyming pair by its ending sound, not its first sound
Names two bicycle parts in English (bell, wheel, seat, pedal)
Says one full sentence about playing outside, like 'I ride my cycle in the park'

misconceptions.belief: Two words rhyme if they start with the same sound
signs: Picks the option with the same first letter
Cannot hear that 'bell' and 'well' end the same

diagnostic.prompt_en: Which word rhymes with 'bell': 'well' or 'ball'?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: 'Bell' ke saath kaunsa word rhyme karta hai — 'well' ya 'ball'? Aakhri awaaz suno.

remediation.representation: Word cards split into start and end chunks (b + ell, w + ell) with the end chunk coloured the same
remediation.moveShape: Say both words slowly, stretch the ending, let the child hear which endings match; then try a new pair

misconceptions.belief: After a number like two or many, the naming word stays the same (no -s)
signs: Counts correctly but never adds the -s sound
Says 'one wheels' or 'two wheel' at random

diagnostic.prompt_en: A bicycle has two ___. Is it 'wheel' or 'wheels'?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Cycle mein do ___ hote hain. 'Wheel' bolenge ya 'wheels'?

remediation.representation: Picture of one wheel and two wheels side by side, the extra /s/ sound shown as a little snake
remediation.moveShape: Child touches one picture and says the word, then the two-picture and hears the hiss at the end; then a new object

misconceptions.belief: 'I am' goes before every action word (from 'main ... hoon'), so 'I am ride' is a sentence
signs: Says 'I am go to the park'
Uses 'am' in every sentence about himself

diagnostic.prompt_en: Which sounds right: 'I ride my cycle.' or 'I am ride my cycle.'?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Kaunsa sahi lagta hai — 'I ride my cycle.' ya 'I am ride my cycle.'?

remediation.representation: Sentence-scramble cards where the 'am' card does not fit next to 'ride'
remediation.moveShape: Build the sentence with cards, read it aloud both ways, let the child hear which one flows; then a new action word

items.prompt_en: Listen: 'bell', 'well'. Do they sound the same at the end?
items.prompt_hi: Suno: 'bell', 'well'. Kya dono ka end same sound karta hai? Yes ya no?
hints: Say both words slowly. What do you hear at the end?
Listen to the last part of each word.
b-ell, w-ell. The ends are the s___?
Yes. Bell and well both end in -ell, so they rhyme.

items.prompt_en: Which word rhymes with 'hill': 'still' or 'hat'?
items.prompt_hi: 'Hill' ke saath kaunsa rhyme karta hai — 'still' ya 'hat'?
hints: Say 'hill' and stretch the end.
Rhyming words end the same, they need not start the same.
h-ill and st-___? Which one ends in -ill?
Still rhymes with hill. Both end in -ill.

items.prompt_en: Listen: 'bell' and 'ball'. They both start with /b/. Do they rhyme?
items.prompt_hi: 'Bell' aur 'ball' — dono /b/ se shuru hote hain. Par kya ye rhyme karte hain?
hints: Rhyme is about the end. Listen to the ends.
One ends in -ell. What does the other end in?
-ell and -all. Are they the same?
No. They start the same but end differently, so they do not rhyme.

items.prompt_en: Clap with me on each beat: 'Ring, ring, goes my ___.' What is the last word?
items.prompt_hi: Mere saath taali bajao: 'Ring, ring, goes my ___.' Aakhri word kya hai?
hints: What on a cycle goes ring, ring?
We press it with our thumb.
It rhymes with 'well': b___.
Ring, ring, goes my bell!

items.prompt_en: In our cycle rhyme we rode up the lane. Where did we ride down?
items.prompt_hi: Hamari cycle wali rhyme mein hum lane ke upar gaye. Neeche kahan se aaye?
hints: Think of the line after the wheels roll well.
It is a high place we ride up and down.
Up the lane and down the h___.
Up the lane and down the hill.

items.prompt_en: Here is a new line: 'Ring, ring, I ride along, singing my happy cycle ___.' Which word fits and rhymes with 'along': 'song' or 'bell'?
items.prompt_hi: Nayi line: 'Ring, ring, I ride along, singing my happy cycle ___.' Kaunsa word fit hoga aur 'along' se rhyme karega — 'song' ya 'bell'?
hints: What do we do when we sing?
Listen to the end of 'along': -ong.
Which word ends in -ong?
Song. Along and song rhyme.

items.prompt_en: A cycle has a round part that rolls on the road. In Hindi it is 'pahiya'. What is it in English? Tap the picture and say it.
items.prompt_hi: Cycle ka 'pahiya' — English mein kya kehte hain? Picture pe tap karo aur bolo.
hints: It goes round and round.
A cycle has two of them.
It starts with /w/: wh___.
Pahiya is 'wheel' in English.

items.prompt_en: Where do you sit on a bicycle: on the seat or on the pedal?
items.prompt_hi: Cycle pe tum kahan baithte ho — seat pe ya pedal pe?
hints: What do your feet push?
Your feet go on the pedals. Where does the rest of you go?
We sit on the s___.
We sit on the seat and push the pedals.

items.prompt_en: Why does a bicycle have a bell?
items.prompt_hi: Cycle mein ghanti kyun hoti hai? Socho, sadak pe kya kaam aati hai?
items.answer: To tell people we are coming so they can move and stay safe
acceptable: so people move out of the way
so people know I am coming
hints: When do you ring the bell?
Think of someone walking in front of your cycle.
We ring it so people ___ we are coming.
The bell tells people we are coming, so they move and nobody gets hurt.

items.prompt_en: Bittu says, 'My bicycle has two wheel.' Something is wrong. How should he say it?
items.prompt_hi: Bittu kehta hai, 'My bicycle has two wheel.' Kuch galat hai. Sahi kaise bolega?
hints: Count the round parts on the cycle.
When there are two, the word changes a little at the end.
Add the snake sound /s/ at the end: wheel___.
Two wheels. More than one wheel needs the /s/ sound.

items.prompt_en: We said 'I ride my cycle.' Now make a sentence like it with 'kite' and 'fly'.
items.prompt_hi: Humne bola 'I ride my cycle.' Ab 'kite' aur 'fly' le kar waisa hi sentence banao.
acceptable: I fly my kite in the park.
hints: Start the way we did: 'I ...'
What do we do with a kite?
I ___ my kite.
I fly my kite.

items.prompt_en: Bittu says, 'I am ride my cycle every day.' Help Bittu say it the right way.
items.prompt_hi: Bittu bolta hai, 'I am ride my cycle every day.' Bittu ki madad karo — sahi kaise bolenge?
items.answer: I ride my cycle every day.
acceptable: I ride my bicycle every day.
hints: Say Bittu's sentence slowly. Does one word not fit?
Look at the small word just before 'ride'.
Take out one word: 'I ___ ride my cycle'?
We say 'I ride my cycle every day' with no 'am'.

items.prompt_en: Your little friend Bittu has never heard our cycle rhyme. Tell him what it is about, and say one line with him.
items.prompt_hi: Bittu ne hamari cycle wali rhyme kabhi nahi suni. Usse batao rhyme kis baare mein hai, aur ek line uske saath bolo.
items.answer: The rhyme is about riding a bicycle: the bell rings, the wheels go round, we ride up the lane and down the hill.
acceptable: It is about riding a cycle and ringing the bell
a child rides a bicycle outside
hints: What is the rhyme about?
What sound does the cycle make, and where does it go?
The rhyme is about riding a ___ ...
It is about riding a bicycle: ring, ring goes the bell, and we ride up and down the hill.

workedExample.problem: Find the rhyming pair: 'Ring, ring, goes my bell, / Round and round the wheels roll well.'
steps: Say the last word of line one: bell.
Say the last word of line two: well.
Stretch the ends: b-ell, w-ell.
The ends sound the same, so bell and well rhyme.
fadedVersion: Say the last word of line one: ___.
Say the last word of line two: ___.
Stretch the ends: b-___, w-___.
The ends sound the ___, so bell and well rhyme.

interestContexts: a new cycle on a birthday
topics.passage:
Ring, ring, goes my bell,
Round and round the wheels roll well.
Up the lane and down the hill,
Pedal fast, then I stand still.
Ring, ring, I ride along,
Singing my happy cycle song.

skills.title: Name things and actions seen in a picture (rope, kite, swing, bat, ball; skip, fly, hide, run)
Say a short sentence about the picture ('This is a ball.', 'She is swinging.')
Answer who, what and where questions about the picture
Talk about my own favourite game with friends

expectations: Names at least three things or games in the picture in English
Uses a full sentence with 'is' (She is swinging / This is a kite)
Uses 'he' for a boy and 'she' for a girl
Says where something is (behind the tree, in the sky)
Says one sentence about a game they like and with whom they play it

misconceptions.belief: A naming word can stand alone after 'This is' (Hindi 'yeh gend hai' has no 'a')
signs: Leaves out 'a' and 'the' in every sentence

diagnostic.prompt_en: Which sounds right: 'This is a ball.' or 'This is ball.'?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Kaunsa sahi lagta hai — 'This is a ball.' ya 'This is ball.'?

remediation.representation: Sentence strip with an empty little box before every naming word, filled by an 'a' card
remediation.moveShape: Point to one object, say the sentence with a tap on the little box; child repeats, then tries a new object

misconceptions.belief: An -ing word alone tells the action ('She swinging'), the 'is' is not needed
signs: Answers 'What is she doing?' with 'Swinging she'

diagnostic.prompt_en: Which one is a full sentence: 'She is swinging.' or 'She swinging.'?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Kaunsa poora sentence hai — 'She is swinging.' ya 'She swinging.'?

remediation.representation: Three word cards She / is / swinging that click together like a train; a missing middle carriage stops the train
remediation.moveShape: Build the train with the child, take out 'is', ask if the train can move; put it back and say it together

misconceptions.belief: 'He' and 'she' can be used for anyone (Hindi 'vo' is the same for boy and girl)
signs: Says 'he' for a girl in the picture
Switches between he and she for the same child

diagnostic.prompt_en: The girl is on the swing. Which is right: 'He is on the swing.' or 'She is on the swing.'?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ladki jhoole pe hai. Kaunsa sahi hai — 'He is on the swing.' ya 'She is on the swing.'?

remediation.representation: Two picture cards, a boy with a blue 'he' tag and a girl with a pink 'she' tag, matched to children in the scene
remediation.moveShape: Child points to each child in the picture and says he or she before saying the action; then a new picture

items.prompt_en: In the picture, a boy is holding a string. At the top, a red patang is high in the sky. What is a patang called in English?
items.prompt_hi: Picture mein ek ladka dhaaga pakad ke khada hai, upar laal patang ud rahi hai. Patang ko English mein kya kehte hain?
hints: Look up in the sky in the picture.
It flies on a string.
It starts with /k/: k___.
A patang is a kite.

items.prompt_en: Two girls are jumping over a long rope. What game are they playing: skipping or cricket?
items.prompt_hi: Do ladkiyan lambi rassi ke upar kood rahi hain. Kaunsa game hai — skipping ya cricket?
hints: What do the girls have in their hands?
Cricket needs a bat. These girls have a rope.
Jumping over a rope is called sk___.
They are skipping.

items.prompt_en: Point to the boy with the bat. What will he hit with the bat?
items.prompt_hi: Bat wale ladke ki taraf ishaara karo. Woh bat se kya maarega?
hints: What do we hit in cricket?
It is small and round.
He hits the b___.
He will hit the ball.

items.prompt_en: Point to the ball and say it fully: 'This is ___ ball.' What small word goes in the gap?
items.prompt_hi: Ball ki taraf ishaara karke poora bolo: 'This is ___ ball.' Beech mein kaunsa chhota word aayega?
hints: Say it slowly. Is something missing?
One tiny word comes before 'ball'.
This is _ ball. The tiny word is just one letter.
This is a ball.

items.prompt_en: Listen to two sentences. 'She is swinging.' 'She swinging.' Which one is the full sentence?
items.prompt_hi: Do sentence suno: 'She is swinging.' aur 'She swinging.' Inmein se poora sentence kaunsa hai?
hints: Say both. Does one feel short?
Count the words in each.
She ___ swinging. What goes in the middle?
She is swinging is the full sentence; it has 'is'.

items.prompt_en: Look at the girl on the swing. Bittu says, 'He is on the swing.' What is wrong? Say it the right way.
items.prompt_hi: Jhoole wali ladki ko dekho. Bittu kehta hai, 'He is on the swing.' Kya galat hai? Sahi bolo.
hints: Is it a boy or a girl on the swing?
For a boy we say 'he'. For a girl we use a different word.
S___ is on the swing.
She is on the swing, because it is a girl.

items.prompt_en: In our picture, a girl in a red frock is hiding. Where is she hiding?
items.prompt_hi: Picture mein laal frock wali ladki chhupi hai. Woh kahan chhupi hai?
hints: Look for the girl in the red frock.
What big green thing is near her?
She is hiding be___ the tree.
She is hiding behind the tree.

items.prompt_en: A boy has his eyes closed and is counting. A girl is hiding behind the tree. Why are his eyes closed?
items.prompt_hi: Ek ladka aankhein band karke gin raha hai, aur ladki ped ke peeche chhupi hai. Uski aankhein band kyun hain?
items.answer: They are playing hide-and-seek, so he must not see where his friends hide
acceptable: so he cannot see them hide
hints: What game needs one child to count?
If his eyes were open, what would he see?
His friends are hiding, so he must not ___.
They are playing hide-and-seek, so he closes his eyes and does not see where they hide.

items.prompt_en: The boy finishes counting: 'eight, nine, ten!' What will he do next?
items.prompt_hi: Ladka ginti khatam karta hai: 'eight, nine, ten!' Ab woh aage kya karega?
items.answer: He will look for his friends
acceptable: he will look for the girl
he will open his eyes and find them
hints: What happens after counting in this game?
His friends are hiding.
He will open his eyes and l___ for them.
He will look for his friends and try to find them.

items.prompt_en: Now a new picture: two boys are running a race. Say one sentence about them, like 'She is swinging.'
items.prompt_hi: Ab nayi picture: do ladke race mein daud rahe hain. Unke baare mein ek sentence bolo, jaise 'She is swinging.'
hints: What are the boys doing?
For two boys we say 'they', not 'he'.
They ___ running.
They are running.

items.prompt_en: Earlier we saw two girls with a long rope. What was their game called?
items.prompt_hi: Pehle humne do ladkiyan lambi rassi ke saath dekhi thi. Unka game kya kehlata hai?
hints: Think back to the girls in the picture.
They jumped and jumped over the rope.
It was skipping.

items.prompt_en: What game do you like to play with your friends? Say: 'I like to play ___.'
items.prompt_hi: Tumhe doston ke saath kaunsa game khelna pasand hai? Bolo: 'I like to play ___.'
acceptable: I like to play with my friends.
hints: Which game makes you happy?
Think of a game in the park or at home.
I like to play ___.
For example: I like to play kho-kho.

items.prompt_en: Your friend Bittu has never played hide-and-seek. Tell him how to play it in two or three short sentences.
items.prompt_hi: Bittu ne kabhi chhupan-chhupai nahi kheli. Usse do-teen chhote sentences mein batao kaise khelte hain.
items.answer: One child closes the eyes and counts; the others hide; then that child looks for them and finds them.
acceptable: one counts, others hide, then he finds them
close your eyes and count, friends hide, then you find them
hints: How does the game start?
What do the other children do while one counts?
First one child counts, then the others ___ ...
One child counts, the others hide, then the counter finds them.

workedExample.problem: Say one sentence about the girl on the swing.
steps: Look: is it a boy or a girl? A girl, so we say 'she'.
What is she doing? Swinging.
Join them with 'is': She is swinging.
Say the whole sentence: She is swinging.
fadedVersion: Look: is it a boy or a girl? A girl, so we say '___'.
What is she doing? ___.
Join them with '___': She is swinging.
Say the whole sentence: She ___ swinging.

interestContexts: playing with cousins at a wedding
topics.passage: Picture (original scene, shown on screen): a park in the evening. Two girls skip with a long rope. A boy flies a red kite. A girl in a red frock hides behind a big tree while a boy counts with his eyes closed. A girl sits on a swing. Three children play cricket with a bat and a ball.

skills.title: Match animals to movement words (hop, fly, swim, crawl, run)
Say the animal rhyme with its beat and do the actions
Hear and say rhyming pairs (hop/stop, swish/wish, one/fun)
Say a sentence about how an animal moves ('A frog hops.')

expectations: Names how at least three animals move: frog hops, bird flies, fish swims, snail crawls
Does the matching action while saying the line
Picks a rhyming pair by its ending sound
Says an animal sentence with the -s ending: 'A frog hops.'

misconceptions.belief: With one animal, the action word stays bare: 'A frog hop'
signs: Never adds -s after he/she/it or one animal

diagnostic.prompt_en: Which sounds right: 'A frog hops.' or 'A frog hop.'?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Kaunsa sahi lagta hai — 'A frog hops.' ya 'A frog hop.'?

remediation.representation: One frog picture with an -s tail on the action card; many frogs with no tail
remediation.moveShape: Child hops one finger-frog and says the sentence with the hiss; then many frogs without it; then a new animal

misconceptions.belief: After 'can', the action word also takes -s: 'A bird can flies'

diagnostic.prompt_en: Which is right: 'A bird can fly.' or 'A bird can flies.'?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Kaunsa sahi hai — 'A bird can fly.' ya 'A bird can flies.'?

remediation.representation: A 'can' card that 'eats' the -s: when it sits before the action card, the -s tail drops off
remediation.moveShape: Say the sentence without 'can' (A bird flies), then slide in 'can' and take away the tail together

misconceptions.belief: 'Walk' (from 'chalna') is the word for any animal moving

diagnostic.prompt_en: How does a snake move? Does a snake walk or crawl?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Saanp kaise chalta hai? English mein — snake walks ya crawls?

remediation.representation: Picture cards of animal feet, fins, wings and a snake's body, each matched to its movement word
remediation.moveShape: Ask what the animal has (legs, wings, fins, no legs), act it out, then pick the word that fits that body

items.prompt_en: How does a fish move in the water: does it swim or fly?
items.prompt_hi: Machhli paani mein kaise chalti hai — swim karti hai ya fly?
hints: Where does a fish live?
Birds fly in the sky. What do fish do in water?
A fish s___.
A fish swims.

items.prompt_en: A frog goes jump, jump, jump on its strong legs. Which word is it: hop or crawl?
items.prompt_hi: Mendhak apne mazboot pairon se jump-jump karta hai. Kaunsa word — hop ya crawl?
hints: Show me with your hand how a frog moves.
Crawl is slow and low. A frog goes up and down.
A frog h___.
A frog hops.

items.prompt_en: Tap the animal that crawls very slowly: a snail, a bird or a fish.
items.prompt_hi: Us jaanwar pe tap karo jo bahut dheere crawl karta hai — snail, bird ya fish.
hints: Which one has no legs and no wings?
It carries a little shell on its back.
The snail crawls very slowly.

items.prompt_en: A dog walks on four legs. A snake has no legs. Does a snake walk or crawl?
items.prompt_hi: Kutta chaar pairon se walk karta hai. Saanp ke pair nahi hote. Snake walks ya crawls?
hints: Can you walk with no legs?
A snake moves on its tummy along the ground.
A snake cr___.
A snake crawls; only animals with legs walk.

items.prompt_en: Clap with me: 'Hop like a frog, hop, hop, ___!' What is the next word?
items.prompt_hi: Taali bajao: 'Hop like a frog, hop, hop, ___!' Agla word kya hai?
hints: Listen to the pattern: hop, hop ...
The same word comes three times.
Hop, hop, h___!
Hop, hop, hop!

items.prompt_en: In our rhyme, which animal did we swim like?
items.prompt_hi: Hamari rhyme mein hum kis jaanwar ki tarah tair rahe the?
hints: Swish, swish, swish ... who says that?
It lives in water.
Swim like a f___.
Swim like a fish.

items.prompt_en: Which word rhymes with 'hop': 'stop' or 'swim'?
items.prompt_hi: 'Hop' ke saath kaunsa rhyme karta hai — 'stop' ya 'swim'?
hints: Say 'hop' and listen to its end.
Rhyming words end the same: -op.
h-op, st-___?
Stop rhymes with hop. Both end in -op.

items.prompt_en: A new line for our rhyme: 'Run like a deer, run, run, run! Running and jumping is so much ___.' Which word fits and rhymes with 'run'?
items.prompt_hi: Rhyme ki nayi line: 'Run like a deer, run, run, run! Running and jumping is so much ___.' Kaunsa word 'run' se rhyme karega aur fit hoga?
hints: How do you feel when you run and jump?
It must end like 'run': -un.
So much f___.
Fun. Run and fun rhyme.

items.prompt_en: Bittu says, 'A frog hop.' Fix it for him.
items.prompt_hi: Bittu kehta hai, 'A frog hop.' Uske liye theek karo.
hints: Say it slowly. Is something missing at the end?
For one frog, the action word gets a little sound.
A frog hop___? Add a hiss.
A frog hops. One frog, so we add -s.

items.prompt_en: Bittu says, 'A bird can flies.' What should he say?
items.prompt_hi: Bittu bolta hai, 'A bird can flies.' Use kya bolna chahiye?
hints: Look at the word after 'can'.
After 'can', the action word stays plain, with no -s.
A bird can f___.
A bird can fly.

items.prompt_en: A rabbit moves like a frog, with big jumps. Say a sentence: 'A rabbit ___.'
items.prompt_hi: Khargosh bhi mendhak ki tarah kood-kood ke chalta hai. Sentence bolo: 'A rabbit ___.'
hints: How does a frog move?
The rabbit moves the same way.
A rabbit h___ ... remember the -s.
A rabbit hops.

items.prompt_en: Why can a fish not walk on the road?
items.prompt_hi: Machhli sadak pe walk kyun nahi kar sakti?
items.answer: Because a fish has no legs; it has fins and lives in water, so it swims
acceptable: fish swim, they do not have legs
hints: What do we need to walk?
Does a fish have legs?
A fish has fins, not ___.
A fish has no legs; it has fins, so it swims in water.

items.prompt_en: Teach Bittu our animal rhyme: tell him which animals we were and how each one moves.
items.prompt_hi: Bittu ko hamari jaanwar wali rhyme sikhao: kaun-kaun se jaanwar bane aur har ek kaise chalta hai.
items.answer: A frog hops, a bird flies, a fish swims and a snail crawls.
acceptable: frog hops, bird flies, fish swims, snail crawls
hints: Which animal came first?
Name the animal that lives in water and the slow one.
A frog ___, a bird ___, a fish ___ ...
A frog hops, a bird flies, a fish swims and a snail crawls.

workedExample.problem: Say how a bird moves, in a full sentence.
steps: What does a bird have? Wings.
With wings, a bird flies.
One bird, so the action word gets -s: flies.
Say it: A bird flies.
fadedVersion: What does a bird have? ___.
With wings, a bird ___.
One bird, so the action word gets ___: flies.
Say it: A bird ___.

topics.passage:
Hop like a frog, hop, hop, hop,
Fly like a bird, and do not stop!
Swim like a fish, swish, swish, swish,
Crawl like a snail, as slow as you wish.
Move like the animals, everyone,
Moving and playing is so much fun!

skills.title: Listen to the story and answer who and what questions
Put the story events in order and retell them with pictures
Use the senses words: see, hear, smell, touch, taste
Say kind words to welcome a new classmate

expectations: Tara is new in the class and cannot see with her eyes
She knows people and things by hearing, touching and smelling
Rohan is kind: he says hello and shares his laddoo
They become good friends
Retells in order with 'first', 'then', 'at the end'

misconceptions.belief: 'He' and 'she' are interchangeable (Hindi 'vo' works for both)
signs: Switches he and she in one retelling

diagnostic.prompt_en: Tara reads with her fingers. Which is right: 'She reads with her fingers.' or 'He reads with his fingers.'?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Tara apni ungliyon se padhti hai. Kaunsa sahi hai — 'She reads with her fingers.' ya 'He reads with his fingers.'?

remediation.representation: Character cards for Tara (she/her) and Rohan (he/his) placed beside each story picture
remediation.moveShape: Before each retelling sentence, child touches the character card and says the matching word first

misconceptions.belief: A story about yesterday uses the action word as it is: 'Rohan share his laddoo'
signs: Uses 'yesterday' but keeps the verb plain

diagnostic.prompt_en: Yesterday Rohan ___ his laddoo. Is it 'shared' or 'share'?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Kal (beete hue din) Rohan ne apna laddoo ___. 'shared' ya 'share'?

remediation.representation: A timeline strip: today on the right, yesterday on the left; past action cards carry an -ed tail
remediation.moveShape: Move the picture to yesterday on the strip, add the -ed tail together, then retell that picture

misconceptions.belief: 'Yesterday' and 'tomorrow' mean the same thing, because Hindi uses 'kal' for both
signs: Pauses or guesses when asked about days

diagnostic.prompt_en: Today is Tuesday. Monday was the day before. Was Monday yesterday or tomorrow?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Aaj Tuesday hai. Monday pichhla din tha. Toh Monday 'yesterday' tha ya 'tomorrow'?

remediation.representation: A three-box day strip: yesterday (arrow back), today (a dot), tomorrow (arrow forward)
remediation.moveShape: Hindi 'kal' has two arrows; walk a finger back for yesterday and forward for tomorrow, then ask a new day

She knew Rohan from his voice.

We hear with our ears.
